newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down despite futures move abroad.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down despite futures move abroad.

text.p: Taiwan share pricss opened sharply higher but closed slightly lower on Thursday as trade turned more volatile due to the launch of offshore Taiwan stock index futures in Singapore and Chicago, brokers said.
The index ended off 8.67 points or 0.12 percent at 7,010.76, off a 7,091.17 high. Turnover was a heavy T$81.73 billion.
Brokers attributed the fall to financials' weakness.

Financials, which jumped two percent in early trade, ended 0.45 percent lower as the bellwether Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- saw their rally slow. All three had risen the daily seven percent limit on Wednesday.
The rally for the Big Three state banks showed signs of slowing as investors focussed on Finance Ministry plans to sell down its holdings of the three, brokers said.

Chang Hwa, whose ministry target price is T$184 per share, ended up T$1 to T$167. First Bank fell T$2 to T$173 -- just below the ministry's target price of T$176 -- while Hua Nan gained T$6 to T$142, still well below its $188 target.
The plan aims to raise T$3.7 billion by selling off Big Three holdings before July to ease a government budget deficit. Several papers carried updated reports of the plan on Thursday.
Brokers said investors believed the ministry plan would offset the three banks' future gains on fears of new flood of shares in the market.
"First Bank immediately faced restriction in further rises," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Brokers noted Taiwan share prices had moved with noticeably more volatility on Thursday, clearly reflecting the launch of offshore Taiwan stock-index futures in Singapore and Chicago.
"At the very beginning, the index movement was volatile due to the addition of several new overseas indices for reference," said Jardine Fleming fund manager George Hou.
"But our hypersensitive local investors should get used to them pretty soon. In the long run, all price movements should return to fundamentals," Hou said.
Brokers said the impact of the futures moves abroad was weaker than expected, probably because Taiwan regulators still forbid local investors to trade the foreign contracts.
"Investors also need time to learn how foreign Taiwan indices may affect our index movements," Yang of National said.
For Friday, a 6,950-7,100 range was seen.
